::: proof

Expanding entry-wise, $\tp{\vb} \matr{S} \vb = \sumjp \sumto{k}{p} s_{jk} \beta_j \beta_k$.
Differentiating component-wise with respect to $\beta_i$ for $i = 1, \ldots, p$:

$$
\ba
\left[\deriv{\vb}(\tp{\vb}\matr{S}\vb)\right]_i
&= \deriv{\beta_i} \sumjp \sumto{k}{p} s_{jk} \beta_j \beta_k
&& \text{(expand quadratic form)} \\
&= \sumto{k}{p} s_{ik} \beta_k + \sumjp s_{ji} \beta_j
&& \text{(product rule for } \beta_i \beta_k \text{)} \\
&= [\matr{S}\vb]_i + [\tp{\matr{S}}\vb]_i
&& \text{(matrix-vector multiplication definition)} \\
&= [(\matr{S} + \tp{\matr{S}})\vb]_i
&& \text{(linearity of matrix multiplication)}
\ea
$$

When $\matr{S}$ is symmetric ($\matr{S} = \tp{\matr{S}}$), $\matr{S} + \tp{\matr{S}} = 2\matr{S}$, so $\deriv{\vb}(\tp{\vb}\matr{S}\vb) = 2\matr{S}\vb$.

:::
